accuracy.evidence: Checked against the AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462 specification 4.1.1.4 to 4.1.1.6: isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons, relative atomic mass is an average value that takes account of the abundance of the isotopes, and Higher tier calculates Ar from percentage abundance. Lab data use textbook abundances (Cl 75/25 gives 35.5, Cu 69/31 gives 63.6, B 20/80 gives 10.8, Br 55/45 gives 79.9).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: the plain mean (predict At 36, halfway; challenge tag mid), weighting the wrong way round (tag swap), equal mass numbers meaning isotopes (¹⁴C and ¹⁴N card and tag sameA), confusing ions with isotopes (¹⁶O and ¹⁶O²⁻, tag ion), taking A or Z as the neutron number or adding them (tiles plus tags A, Z, sum), and heavier isotopes reacting differently (predict and tags neut and mass).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagisot is built around a beam balance: abundance bars stand at each isotope's mass on a number line and the learner drags the pivot until the beam stops tilting, then reverses it by dragging an abundance split. Lesson 109's flagnuc builds a single atom particle by particle, so there is no nucleus builder here; the sorts and the A − Z bar are new, and the shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Driving the lab: the beam tilts towards the heavier side in proportion to the turning effect, so the learner finds the balance point and sees it sits nearer the commoner isotope before any formula appears; the done message then shows (75 × 35 + 25 × 37) ÷ 100 = 35.5. The neutron bar splits A into a Z part and a hidden N part, so A − Z is shown as a picture, and each wrong tile names what that number really is.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab tests: same mass number means isotopes, ¹⁴C has 14 or 20 neutrons, heavier atoms react differently, chlorine balances at 36 halfway, and bromine at 79.9 has equal amounts. A.reveal quotes the learner's guess in every done message, so a wrong guess is shown against the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Four rotating challenge questions with nine tagged wrong answers, each with its own worked fix in because(), for example 21 is a plain mean, weight it: (90 × 20 + 10 × 22) ÷ 100 = 20.2. In-lab slips also explain: a wrong sort says Z is 6 and 7, so different elements, even with the same mass number, and a wrong tile says that is the mass number A, take Z away.

readability.evidence: Learner text stays within the learner grade limits using short sentences and defined terms (To find the neutrons, take Z away from A.), and the adult text names the specification points, atomic number, mass number, neutron number, nuclide, nuclear notation, electron arrangement, percentage abundance and weighted mean without padding.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and overlap with Atomic number and mass number and Charges and masses of subatomic particles is under 12 percent. Each learner paragraph does one job (what an isotope is, reading the notation, why chemistry matches, the weighted mean), and the adult paragraphs give the specification home, a glossary, named mistakes with an ion caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light: the six nuclide-pair cards are full-width rows with readable superscripts and subscripts, the neutron bar and four answer tiles fill the width, the beam, bars and pivot fit with tick labels clear, and the abundance split bar is a full-width drag target with plus and minus 5% button twins below.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all Show me tasks completed and the challenge rendered. Every drag has a button twin (Pick a card and Put in each box, N = tiles, pivot nudges of 0.1 and 0.5 with aria-labels, plus and minus 5% abundance), and the canvas aria-label speaks each worked result.
